newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian ministry urges higher credit for exporters.
newsitem.headline: Indian ministry urges higher credit for exporters.

text.p: India's commerce ministry has suggested to the central bank that it raise the minimum credit limit to exporters by banks to 15 percent from 10 percent of total credit made available to industry, an official said.
"The suggestion is pending with the finance ministry. They should decide soon," a ministry official, who asked not to be named, told Reuters on Monday.
The availability of more credit for exporters is expected to make exports more competitive, the official said.
Indian exports rose sharply after India launched sweeping economic reforms in 1991. Exports have risen at around 20 percent a year in the past three years.

The commerce ministry official said the Reserve Bank of India had also been asked to see whether exporters could be granted loans at interest rates lower than commercial rates, currently around 17 percent.
